question: Does the unchanged inverse-diameter RMS law pass the newly acquired Kodak Research multi-aperture photographic-film tables when normalized independently at 48 micrometres per density group?

branch_rule.pass: Retain inverse-area aperture scaling as measured historical-photographic compatibility for a generic reference compiler; P4BB Kodak 250D amplitude remains separate and spatial NPS stays unidentified.
branch_rule.fail: Close independent-cell spatial interpretation across both measured sources; retain only analytic P4BB cell moments and do not fit an exponent.

forbidden: fit or substitute an aperture exponent after scoring
omit low-density, large-aperture or film-specific hard rows
transfer historical B&W amplitudes into the Kodak 250D bundle
claim microscopic geometry, measured NPS, colour-stock calibration or product rendering
claim_ceiling: No-fit inverse-diameter aperture-law compatibility across four historical photographic films and 23 density groups; not Kodak 250D amplitude transfer, modern stock/process/scanner calibration, microscopic geometry, full NPS or product evidence.
